Name: SupporterMod
Description: v0.28.1 - Wings sweep BACKWARD now. 0.28.0 got the mirroring right - both wings finally matched - but had the sweep pointing the wrong way: seen from above they curved forward around the torso, which is why the inner segments were buried in the player's back. Both Y signs flipped, and that is the whole change, which is the point worth recording. Splitting rotation by axis in 0.28.0 is what made this a one-character fix instead of another rebuild: the lean and the sweep were separable, the mirroring was already proven correct by the two wings matching, and the arc was carried by position rather than by rotation - so the only thing left that could be wrong was a single sign, and flipping it could not disturb anything else. Compare that with 0.27.0, where a wrong sign collapsed the whole wing into planks and took three builds to unpick, because rotation was doing four jobs at once. The roots also moved back one unit to z-11, level with where the vanilla cape panel hangs, for a little more clearance behind the shoulder blades. Same item id, same price, same slot. 102 tests. ---  v0.28.0 - ROTATION, back on the wings and split by axis - the piece of understanding that was missing the first time. 0.27.0 angled every segment about Y and mirrored the sign for the opposite wing; one side swept back, the other did not, and 0.27.2 pulled rotation out entirely rather than guess again. The reason it failed is that THE TWO AXES DO NOT MIRROR THE SAME WAY. Reflecting through the YZ plane - which is what the opposite wing is - leaves a rotation about X UNCHANGED but flips the sign of a rotation about Y. So the two are now separated: the backward LEAN uses an X-axis rotation with the SAME quaternion on both wings, where there is no handedness to get wrong at all, while the outward SWEEP is the mirrored Y pair, applied to the three outer segments so it accumulates to about forty degrees down the wing. The lean is 10 degrees back on the root, which tips the whole wing with it since children inherit their parent's transform. AND THE ARC IS STILL POSITION-DRIVEN, deliberately: rotation now shapes the wing but does not hold it up, so a sign error would tilt the wings oddly rather than collapse them into planks the way it did before. That is the difference between adding rotation blind and adding it once the geometry underneath is already known good. Same item id, same 600 tokens, same chest slot. 102 tests. ---  v0.27.3 - Wings pushed behind the arms and given an actual arc. Two faults from the live look, and the second explains why they kept reading as planks. THE ARMS PASSED THROUGH THEM because the wings sat at z-7, which is arm-swing depth - close enough to the body that a walking animation drove straight through the inner segment. They now start at z-10, level with where the vanilla cape panel hangs, and step back another 2 per segment, so the whole wing is behind the arc an arm travels through. AND THEY WERE FLAT: each segment rose only 3 while shrinking 3 in height, so the tops stayed level and the bottoms crept up - which is not a wing, it is a tapered plank, and that is exactly what the screenshots showed. Segments now RISE MORE THAN THEY SHRINK - steps of 7, 7 and 6 against heights of 20, 17, 13 and 10 - so the wing arcs upward from below the shoulder to well above it, which is the line that makes a wing read as a wing rather than a shelf. Slightly narrower and taller overall (14x20 root instead of 16x18) for the same reason: the earlier proportions were wider than they were tall once four segments were laid end to end. Sheet re-cut to match. Still no rotation - the arc is built from position alone, so both sides remain identical by construction. Same item id. 102 tests. ---  v0.27.2 - Wings: the two sides disagreed, and the sweep no longer uses rotation. From behind, one wing showed as a broad panel and the other as narrow stripes - they were not the same shape. THE CAUSE was an assumption inside the 0.27.0 build: each segment was angled with an orientation quaternion, and the opposite wing simply had that sign flipped, on the belief that mirroring a rotation mirrors the sweep. It does not follow from the sign alone - one wing swept back and the other did not, which is exactly what a broad face versus an edge-on face looks like. Rather than guess the handedness a second time and spend another live test on it, THE SWEEP IS NOW BUILT FROM POSITION: each segment steps back in z as it steps out in x, which is mirror-symmetric by construction and cannot disagree between sides. Rotation remains available and still worth having - a real angle would beat a staircase - but it needs a probe that can tell the two directions apart before it goes back in, which is the same lesson the scrolling attempt taught: a test both answers pass proves nothing. HEIGHT, THIRD TIME: y+4 put them at the head, y-12 put them at the waist, and they now anchor at y-8, across the back where a wing attaches. Segments and sheet re-cut to match (16x18 root, 128x128 sheet); UV mirroring dropped as well, since one asymmetry at a time is enough while the geometry is in question. Same item id, so wings already held wear the new shape. 102 tests. ---  v0.27.1 - Wings rebuilt after their first live look, which read as EARS rather than wings - small tan flaps beside the head, mostly lost in the hair. Three faults, and the size was only one of them. TOO SMALL AND TOO HIGH: segments grew from 14x16 to 18x22 at the root, and the anchor dropped from y+4 to y-12 so they sit ACROSS THE BACK instead of level with the head. The first version put them where a cape's collar is, which is why they looked like they belonged to the haircut. THREE SEGMENTS READ AS A BLOB: four with a real taper reads as a wing even in silhouette, which is what anybody sees from more than a few blocks away. AND THE TEXTURE WAS TOO SUBTLE TO SURVIVE THE SIZE: at eighteen pixels across, a smooth gradient and one-pixel feather hints just look like dirt. Primaries now alternate light and shadowed as whole feathers, the quills are dark and run the full drop, the leading edge is a hard amber band and the outermost tip is solid gold - the parts that carry at distance. The sheet grew to 128x128 to hold the bigger faces. Geometry, price and slot are otherwise unchanged: same item id, so wings already in an inventory simply wear the new shape. Every first-of-its-kind model this plugin has shipped has needed exactly one pass like this - the crown, the cowboy brim, the trainers - and the lesson each time is the same: authored art is judged in game at the size it actually renders, never on the sheet. 102 tests. ---  v0.27.0 - WINGS, and the assumption that parked them for months was wrong. They were held back on the belief that blockymodel boxes are axis-aligned and angled wings therefore impossible - every self-authored piece so far (crown, cowboy hat, trainers, shades) is a stack of squares because of it. Nodes carry an ORIENTATION QUATERNION, vanilla uses non-identity values throughout its own models, and the Cape_Long back panel this plugin has shipped since 0.9.0 sits at a slight tilt the whole time. One grep answered what a months-old assumption had closed off, which is the lesson: a thing parked as impossible deserves re-checking before it is parked again. EACH WING IS THREE NESTED SEGMENTS, every one rotated a little further about Y than its parent, so the sweep ACCUMULATES down the wing the way a real one does - nesting composes transforms, so no quaternion arithmetic was needed to combine the angles. The right wing mirrors the left's UV on its front and back faces only, so the feather direction reverses rather than repeating. Feathered and pale rather than dark and membranous: cream primaries, a warm amber leading edge and gold tips, picking up the same accent as the cape emblem and the hat buckle, because this is the most expensive thing in the shop and should read as light from a distance. CHEST SLOT, 600 TOKENS - the flagship price, two months of tenure or a fortnight of quests. They share the slot with capes, so it is wings OR a cape, never both, and the Wardrobe section is renamed BACK and holds both so the choice is visible in one row. THEY DO NOT FLY, said in the item description as well as the delivery message: a wearable that looked like a movement perk on a faction server would be the first thing anybody assumed was pay-to-win. One design until it has been seen in game - the same discipline the cape and the hats followed, and every first-of-its-kind model here has needed a tuning pass. 102 tests. ---  v0.26.3 - FIX: the restart duplicate, properly this time - the 0.26.2 sweep was looking in the right place at the wrong moment. THE MISSING FACT: entities in UNLOADED CHUNKS do not exist in the ECS, so nothing can find them. The boot sweep ran seconds after startup, before anybody had logged in, when the leftover pet's chunk was not loaded - it dutifully scanned the world and found nothing, logged nothing, and the player then joined, their chunks loaded, the old pet appeared, and the auto-spawn added a second. The sweep now runs WHERE THE ENTITY IS VISIBLE: immediately before spawning a pet for a player, which is precisely the moment their chunks have loaded and a leftover from a previous server life becomes real to the ECS. A slow periodic pass every 60 seconds backs it up for anything that loads later. THE SECOND FAULT, from the same logs: 'Pet shutdown: removed 0 pet(s)' was printed with a pet plainly standing in the world, which means that by the time a plugin stops, its entity refs are already dead or the stores are gone - synchronous removal at shutdown is not enough and never was. That line now reports tracked, removed AND unreachable separately, because 'removed 0' could not distinguish 'nothing was tracked' from 'everything tracked was already beyond reach', and those call for opposite fixes. Anything counted unreachable is explicitly the next session's sweep to collect. /supporter petsweep is unchanged and still clears a world on demand. 102 tests. ---  v0.26.2 - FIX: pets doubling after a restart, and a sweep command to clear the ones already loose. THE CAUSE was the one case none of the previous guards covered. A pet that outlives the server - a crash, a kill -9, a shutdown removal that silently failed, or a chunk that was simply not loaded when shutdown ran - is still standing in the world when the server comes back, but the tracking map starts empty, so the auto-spawn gives the owner a fresh one and they end up with two. The 0.22.3 despawn timer cannot catch this either: the DespawnComponent does not come back with a persisted entity, so the leftover has no timer at all. THE FIX IS A SWEEP RATHER THAN MORE BOOKKEEPING: the first tick in each world walks the world's entities, finds everything wearing a SupporterPet_ role, and removes whatever the plugin is not tracking. At boot that is all of them, which is exactly right - no pet legitimately exists before a player has logged in and been given one. It runs on the world thread, once per world, and skips tracked pets by reference so a live pet is never touched. This is deliberately not UUID bookkeeping: it does not care how a stray came to exist or whether we ever knew about it, which means it also covers failed removals and bugs not yet written. /SUPPORTER PETSWEEP clears strays from the world you are standing in, on demand. That is the kill stick, as a command rather than an item: pets carry 1000 health precisely so nobody can casually kill someone's companion, and a weapon that could would need combat wiring on an entity built without any - while this clears leftovers instantly and cannot miss one that wandered off. Safe with players online, since anything owned is skipped. 102 tests. ---  v0.26.1 - SCROLLING REVERTED, and the fault was the probe rather than the feature. TopScrolling does NOT preserve absolute anchors: it REFLOWS its children, laying each one after the last, so every screen came apart - Shop chips stepping diagonally down and to the right, stat cards stretched into empty bands, the About callout separated from its own text. Reverted whole; the panel is exactly the 0.25.0 layout again. THE REAL MISTAKE IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FEATURE: the probe that cleared this was NOT A DISCRIMINATING TEST. Twelve rows, forty pixels apart, all at the same x - which is precisely what a vertical flow layout produces too. Both hypotheses passed it identically, so it could only ever have returned 'yes'. A probe has to be built to tell the candidates APART, not to look like success: varied x positions and uneven gaps would have shown the reflow in one glance, and the next attempt at this will use exactly that. The row ceilings stay, which is the cost of being wrong here, and it is a cheap one - laying out to fit has worked all week. What remains true and proven: the mode is accepted by the client and the wheel does scroll, so scrolling IS reachable for a screen designed as a flow from the start. That is a redesign of how content is built, not a flag to set, and it is not worth it while everything fits. 102 tests. ---  v0.25.1 - THE SCROLLING PROBE: /supporter uitest 4 and 5, the last unknown in the panel stack. HyUI exposes TopScrolling as a layout mode and ships a default scrollbar style, but NOTHING INSIDE HYUI EVER USES EITHER - the only reference to 'Scrolling' anywhere in the library is the enum that names it - so the behaviour belongs entirely to the client and cannot be learned from the source. That is precisely the shape of unknown that has cost this project two disconnects, so it gets a probe rather than a guess. TWO QUESTIONS, AND THE SECOND MATTERS MORE: does it scroll, and does a layout mode REARRANGE ITS CHILDREN? Every screen in this panel is positioned absolutely, so a mode that auto-stacks would not add a scrollbar to the design, it would rewrite the layout. The probe answers both in one look: twelve numbered rows, forty pixels apart, inside a 260px viewport they overflow by nearly double. Evenly spaced rows mean absolute anchors survive; bunched or stacked rows mean the mode is unusable here whatever its scrolling does. Variant 5 adds HyUI's own ScrollbarStyle.defaultStyle() rather than an invented one, so a failure there points at the scrollbar rather than the mode. Nothing else changed - the panel does not use scrolling yet and will not until this answers. 102 tests. ---  v0.25.0 - THE REDESIGN IS THE PANEL: /supporter now opens it for everyone, and buying something finally looks like buying something. CHIPS REFRESH IN PLACE: a purchased Shop chip flips to its owned styling - green text, green wash, 'name . owned' - the moment the purchase lands, and a claimed quest's button becomes its own CLAIMED receipt so the row cannot be clicked twice and appear to do nothing. Only the clicked chip is touched, and that is this design's doing rather than restraint: prices here never depend on the balance, so no other chip can go stale - the old panel had to rewrite every row precisely because each one showed how much more you needed. THE WARDROBE IS THE HONEST EXCEPTION: it builds only what you own, so there is no hidden chip waiting to be revealed, and gear, pet and skin purchases now say plainly that reopening will show it rather than pretending otherwise. Keeping locked chips built-and-hidden is what left those sections with two blank rows in the first place, and a gap on every visit is a worse trade than a sentence after a purchase. THE SWITCHOVER KEEPS THE OLD PANEL AS A FALLBACK rather than deleting it: /supporter tries the redesign, falls back to the original panel if it fails to build, and falls back to chat if HyUI is missing entirely. Three rungs, because a player whose panel breaks should lose the new look, not the feature - the same reasoning that has kept the chat output alive under every UI this plugin has shipped. /supporter uitest old opens the original for comparison. 102 tests. ---  v0.24.1 - Two layout faults from the first full look at the redesign. THE WARDROBE'S HOLES: the Pets and Body Skins sections sat above a wide gap, because locked items were built-and-hidden and their invisible chips still reserved two grid rows each. That trick exists so a Shop purchase can reveal a chip without reopening the panel - and this panel does not refresh chips anyway, by the deliberate choice made when it was written - so locked items are simply not built here now, and every section is exactly as tall as what it holds. The Wardrobe has meant what-you-own since 0.19.2; now it is also shaped like it. THE ABOUT TAB ATE AN ADMIN'S OWN COPY: price cards were a fixed 260px, so a third line reading 'Every 30 days of support earns 100 shop tokens' truncated to 'earns 100...' - and the panel then printed its own hardcoded version of that same sentence directly underneath. Cards now share the width evenly and wrap, and the hardcoded duplicate is gone: priceLines is free text the admin writes, and nothing in this panel may quietly swallow it. Everything else from the first look was confirmed working: all eight tabs switch, purchases and claims land, the chat preview follows the title and colour live, quest progress bars read correctly, and the log stayed clean throughout. 102 tests. ---  v0.24.0 - THE WHOLE PANEL, REDESIGNED: all eight screens on the flat shell, still behind /supporter uitest full while the live panel serves /supporter untouched. Status, Perks, Shop, Quests, Trails, Chat, Wardrobe and About, every one of them rebuilt as flat surfaces, hairline cards and clickable chips, with the left rail carrying identity, tenure meter, navigation and the token wallet. TAB SWITCHING IS OURS, NOT HYUI'S: TabNavigationBuilder lays its tabs out horizontally and this design needs a vertical rail, so all eight screens are built up front and a switch is a set of visibility edits - the same editById plus updatePage mechanism every interaction here already used, which is proven, rather than a layout mode that is not. Every action came across: buying trails, gear, pets and skins; claiming quests; wearing trails and the hide-others toggle; the chat title field with its load-bearing no-op listener and the colour swatches, now with a LIVE PREVIEW card the old panel never had; wardrobe delivery, pet selection and skin changes. Quest rows gained real progress bars, which is the thing a number alone could never show. A BUG CAUGHT IN REVIEW, not live, and worth the changelog because it is this codebase's oldest trap: the Wardrobe's section headings were routed through a helper that called addChild and discarded the result. addChild is IMMUTABLE - the child is silently dropped - so all five headings would have rendered as nothing at all, with no error anywhere. Inlined and reassigned. What is deliberately NOT here: nothing scrolls. TopScrolling exists as a layout mode and would retire the row ceilings this plugin keeps fighting, but it is unproven, and this week established exactly what an unproven UI value costs - a disconnect, not a glitch. Every screen is laid out to fit 788px instead, and scrolling is the next experiment rather than this one. Purchases update the wallet and the notice line but leave the clicked chip alone until the panel is reopened; rewriting one chip mid-grid is the partial refresh that has produced stale UI here three times. 102 tests. ---  v0.23.3 - THE SPIKE PASSED: the redesigned Status screen renders in game, and the flat look holds up - rail, nav, stat cards, collection grid and wallet all as specced, with a clean log and no client complaint. Two defects the first live look exposed, both fixed here. COLLECTION CHIPS GO ONE PER ROW: two-up chips were 83px wide and truncated jack-sparrow to 'jack-sparro...' even after shrink-to-fit bottomed out at 9px - names in this plugin run to twelve characters, so each chip now takes the card's full width, three at most, with a '+N more' line under. THE TENURE METER MEANT NOTHING: it measured remaining against max(90, remaining), which is 1 for anybody past ninety days, so it sat pinned at full for every supporter who would ever look at it. It now measures remaining against LIFETIME days - 539 of 630 reads 85%, renewing pushes it back up, letting it lapse empties it - which is what the design's 85.5% mock was showing all along. What the spike proves beyond the look: colour-only patches composite correctly over the scene blur, 8-digit alpha behaves, absolute layout at 1180x788 lands where it is told, and a 40-plus element screen opens with no lag. What it does not answer, and the next tab will: whether the body can SCROLL, since the live panel's twelve-row ceiling exists only because nothing has ever scrolled. 102 tests. ---  v0.23.2 - THE PRIMITIVE WAS THERE ALL ALONG: a patch style with a colour and NO texture. new HyUIPatchStyle().setColor("#0a0f17") - that is how HyUI's own DefaultStyles draws every flat surface it owns, and it was sitting in the jar this plugin has compiled against since 0.8.0. Two builds and two disconnects were spent slicing an 8x8 block of white out of a client texture to achieve what one call does natively. THE LESSON, and it is the useful part: when an API appears to lack a primitive, read how its own defaults are built before inventing a workaround - the workaround is not just longer, it fails in ways the intended path never would. BONUS, and it removes a whole compromise from 0.23.0: the DefaultStyles literals include #000000D1 and #00000000, so colours take 8-DIGIT ALPHA and really composite. The design's rgba() surfaces now port across exactly as written - white .028 for the rail, .09 for hairlines, .018 for cards, the accent at .10 and .12 for washes - instead of being pre-blended against an assumed background, which also means a surface over the scene blur behaves correctly rather than approximately. The probe drops from five texture-slicing variants to three: colour-only, colour-only with alpha, and a tinted Popup nine-patch as the fallback, each still the only styled element in its panel. The Status screen behind /supporter uitest full is rebuilt on the new primitive; the live panel is untouched, as it has been throughout. 102 tests. ---  v0.23.1 - FIX: the redesign spike DISCONNECTED the player, and the correction is bigger than the bug. Opening /supporter uitest dropped the client with 'CustomUI Set command couldn't set value. Selector: #HYUUIDFlatRoot395.Background'. THE LESSON: a texture the client cannot resolve does NOT degrade to an unstyled element - the property set FAILS, and a failed set drops the player out of the server. 0.23.0's changelog said the opposite in as many words, and that false comfort is exactly what made it acceptable to ship four unverified texture paths in one panel; the probe strip meant to identify the good path was killed by the first bad one and reported nothing. Every texture path must now be one that provably exists as a file, because the cost of a wrong one is a disconnect. THE SECOND MISTAKE was method, not fact: 0.23.0 changed three things at once - a new texture path, area slicing and setColor - so the failure named none of them. The fill texture moves to Common/CircularProgressBarMask.png, a base-named file in the same client directory as the Popup and Button textures this plugin has used live for months, carrying a solid 8x8 block of pure opaque white at (113,39) verified pixel by pixel; ColorPickerFill was never a file, only a @2x variant. And the probe is rebuilt as five ONE-VARIABLE-AT-A-TIME tests run individually - /supporter uitest 1 through 5, each a bare panel whose only styled element is the construct under test, stepping down from the full primitive to a proven nine-patch with nothing but a tint - so whichever one drops the connection names the culprit exactly. /supporter uitest with no argument lists them and says plainly that a wrong one disconnects. The Status screen is still there behind /supporter uitest full, and the live panel is untouched throughout. 102 tests. ---  v0.23.0 - SPIKE: THE PANEL REDESIGN, Status screen only. /supporter uitest, admin-only and additive - /supporter still opens the live panel, untouched, so a half-converted UI is never in front of players. THE PRIMITIVE THAT MAKES THE DESIGN POSSIBLE: HyUI offers no solid-colour rectangle, so one is assembled. The client ships ColorPickerFill, whose centre holds a 16x16 block of PURE OPAQUE WHITE - verified pixel by pixel against the asset extract, not assumed - and HyUIPatchStyle can both slice a sub-region of a texture and tint it. Slice the white block, tint it, stretch it: a flat rectangle in any hex. Every surface, hairline, card and meter in the new shell is one of those, which is a different way of drawing from the live panel entirely (that one tints vanilla nine-patches). NO ALPHA: setColor takes a hex, and the design is written in rgba() overlays, so every translucent surface is PRE-BLENDED against its known background - exact rather than approximate, but it means a surface cannot float over an unpredictable backdrop and stay right. THE PROBE: ColorPickerFill ships only as @2x while every other texture this plugin uses has a base-name twin, so whether the client resolves the base name is genuinely unknown. Rather than guess, the spike draws four labelled swatches, one per candidate path; whichever blocks appear name the winner. A texture that fails to resolve draws nothing rather than erroring, so the worst case is a panel with no surfaces and a strip that says why. WHAT THE DESIGN ASKS FOR THAT CANNOT SHIP, recorded so it is not re-litigated: rounded corners (rectangles are rectangles), gradients (only stacked bands), glows and shadows, eased transitions and the 1px hover lift, and the two Google fonts - fonts are client-side and a server asset pack cannot add one, so the type hierarchy is carried by size, weight, case and letter spacing, which is most of what that typography was doing anyway. Borders cost four elements each, and that - not the colours - is the expensive part of the port. The nav is deliberately inert: this spike is about whether flat surfaces READ WELL in game at 1180x788, and wiring eight tabs before knowing that would be wasted work. 102 tests. ---  v0.22.4 - The last overflow: the Wardrobe skins rack. The 0.22.3 pass moved the PETS rack to eight columns but left the skins rack at six, and the arithmetic it missed is simple: thirteen skins plus off is fourteen buttons, a third row at six columns, and off rendered below the panel - the screenshot showed it floating outside. The skins rack now matches the pets rack exactly: eight per row at the tab bar's 106 width, off leading, fourteen buttons in two rows, and the Wardrobe genuinely sits at twelve rows for the first time since the pet catalogue grew. Nothing else changed. 102 tests. ---  v0.22.3 - FIX: a stray bunny, and the lesson that closes the pet lifecycle for good. The live report was a photo of TWO bunnies. The mechanism is the one the raid work documented and this plugin only three-quarters honoured: store.removeEntity CAN SILENTLY FAIL - most often when the entity's chunk has unloaded, which is precisely when a teleport-catchup or a world-change cleanup fires - and the code then dropped its tracking unconditionally, so the old bunny survived untracked while a fresh one spawned beside the owner. Rather than trying to verify every removal path perfectly forever, EVERY PET NOW CARRIES A DEAD-MAN'S SWITCH: an engine DespawnComponent set 120 seconds out and re-armed by the same once-a-second stamp that drives the following. A pet the plugin loses track of - failed removal, chunk unload, kill -9, a crash, a bug not yet met - is collected by the ENGINE within two minutes with no plugin code in the loop. Correctness no longer depends on the bookkeeping being perfect, which is the only kind of correctness that survives contact with a live server. Removal paths also verify afterwards and log when a removal did not take, so the log tells the story the next time instead of a screenshot. THE ONE ALREADY LOOSE predates the timer and cannot be reached retroactively - it cannot fight and drops nothing; whack it (1000 health, a minute's work) or leave it as server fauna. ALSO CONFIRMED from the same photo: the little nubs between the bunny's ears are the vanilla Horns DefaultAttachment - the jackalope was shipping all along. AND THE LAYOUT PASS, from the same batch of screenshots: the fifteen-pet catalogue broke three things at once. The Perks pets roster wrapped onto the quests line (now a count, not a roster); the Wardrobe overflowed the panel bottom, body-skin buttons rendering outside it (the pets rack goes eight per row at the tab bar's 106 width, two rows, and the tab returns to twelve rows); and every grid showed scattered islands, because buttons are positioned at build time and hiding the owned ones left holes wherever they sat. EVERY GRID NOW BUILDS COMPACT: visible buttons first, hidden after - Shop grids list unowned first, Wardrobe racks owned first, and 'no pet' leads its rack. A purchase mid-session still hides in place until reopen, which reads fine; permanent holes did not. The Shop's gear-and-pets grid tightens to six per row at 144 (the longest label, squirrel at 250, still renders full-size) bringing that tab to twelve rows too - the notice line was overlapping the last skins row at thirteen. A new guard asserts no name is ever both gear and pet, because the merged grid routes clicks by catalogue. 102 tests. ---  v0.22.2 - SIX MORE PETS AND TWO OF THEM FREE: the catalogue reaches fifteen. THE FREE PAIR - chick and piglet, cost 0 - completes the pattern every other catalogue follows: every supporter has a companion the moment they subscribe, tokens buy the menagerie. Paid additions: rat 250, gecko 300, lamb 350, goat kid 350. THE APPEARANCE-ID CHECK EARNED ITS KEEP: three of the six differ from their role filenames (Chicken_Chick's appearance is Chick, Pig_Piglet's is Piglet, Sheep_Lamb's is Lamb) - a guessed id is a role that fails validation and never spawns; and the nameplate translation keys follow the ROLE names, not the appearances, which was caught and fixed the same way. LAYOUT: thirteen priced pets need three grid rows, so Gear and Pets merged into one Shop section under one header - the saved header row is what keeps the tab at its 13-row ceiling, and they were one story anyway: the Wardrobe is where both get worn. The whole gear-and-pets grid runs five per row at 176 wide, and the Wardrobe pets rack grows to three six-column rows for sixteen buttons. Free pets never appear in the Shop (nothing to buy) and are always visible in the Wardrobe for supporters, cost-0-is-owned, the standing rule. Fliers still wait for their pettest. 102 tests. ---  v0.22.1 - SIX MORE PETS, hours after the first three went live-verified (the bunny followed, persisted and came back after a relog on the first try). Squirrel 250, mouse 250, frog 300, duck 300, meerkat 400, tortoise 400 - a nine-pet catalogue, every one a WALKER on the exact recipe the bunny proved; the fliers (owl, parrot, crow) wait deliberately, because a flying rig on a Walk motion controller is an unanswered question and pettest exists to answer it before players spend tokens on it. All six appearance ids verified against the vanilla roles before shipping; the tortoise and duck walk at 6 rather than 7 because a waddle should waddle, and the 40-block teleport-to-heel covers what short legs cannot. LAYOUT PAID FOR THE ROSTER: the Shop's pets grid goes five per row at 176 wide (14-character labels render full-size, and 5x176+4x8 is 912 exactly - flush with the content width), taking the blank row under the balance to stay inside the 13-row ceiling; the Wardrobe pets row becomes a six-column grid because nine pets plus no-pet stopped fitting one row. Each new pet still gets a pettest look before players are pointed at it - the catalogue guard test covers the new names automatically, and prices land in live configs through the usual per-key backfill. 102 tests. ---  v0.22.0 - PETS ARE A PERK. The spike passed the same day it shipped - all three rigs animate on a Generic role, follow through the engine's own A*, teleport to heel past 40 blocks, and the shutdown log printed its removal line - so /supporter pet <bunny|fox|penguin|off> is now the real thing: the choice persists in the identity table (schema V8), and the SAME one-second tick that does the following also does the login re-spawn, the world-change re-spawn and the killed-pet recovery, because they are all one mechanism - if your identity names a pet and none is live where you are, one appears beside you. A cosmetic must not be killable in any way that matters.
